top.line: Marconi's observation desk, built as a working vault
top.para: Francesco Marconi argues journalism's advantage will come from how it observes the world. His INMA slides were built as a seventeen-page vault app with 12 families and 78 event types, a six-entity ontology, sixteen records yielding seventeen observations, and a tracker. The records are deliberately synthetic, and anyone with the read key can open and copy it.

in-short.line: The deck became a vault of working, synthetic observations
in-short.para: Marconi's deck is a design of atlas, ontology, observation history, workflow and tracker, so it was built: 78 event types, 6 entities, 16 records and 17 observations, each a subject, change, time and evidence. A fictional campus avoids fake records under real names. Five graphs show the knowledge, and the app can be reused.

argument.line: Journalism is delta science: what changed, and for whom
argument.para: Marconi, of AppliedXL and formerly The Wall Street Journal, says journalism's advantage will come from observation, calling it delta science and requiring an atlas of events, a map of actors and a persistent evidenced record. This site already works similarly; the deck adds defining in advance what counts as a change, with an observable signal.

desk.line: Each of the eleven slides became a working page
desk.para: The data-centre example became a desk following the deck in order: 13 sources and 78 event types, a before-and-after landscape, actors and their interests, the full atlas with definitions and signals, an ontology of six entities and six verbs, seventeen observations from November 2025 to October 2026, the workflow, three queues and the tracker.

found.line: Comparing records revealed a larger permit and fewer jobs
found.para: The air permit grew from up to 5.2 GW applied to 6.1 GW issued, 17% more. Promised jobs fell from 140 to 120. The first 1 GW slipped from 2027 to 2028 after an acquisition, and annual water use stayed undisclosed. Two observations became alerts and one a draft, with no clever model needed.

graphs.line: One graph is drawn five ways, including in time
graphs.para: The atlas, ontology and observation history are views of one graph. A fractal graph opens from the question down to records, a radial view shows all levels, a bipartite graph links records to observations, and a delta chain shows comparisons. The time-played knowledge graph shows edges appearing and moving, each with a date and source.

ai.line: Models make observing cheap; journalists still define and judge
ai.para: Reading every registry and filing used to be expensive, and models make it cheap. They do not replace defining what matters, checking before publication or judging what to report. The vault's workflow follows one cycle: an investor presentation is matched to a milestone revision, compared with April, checked by a person and becomes an alert.

synthetic.line: Real project, fictional twin, so no fake records circulate
synthetic.para: The deck's example is Pacifico Energy's real GW Ranch in Pecos County, Texas, permitted for 7.65 GW of gas-fired generation. Publishing invented permits under real company and agency names would undermine an evidence-based newsroom, so the vault uses Mesa Ranch in Caliche County, with synthetic marked on every record and the first screen.

vault.line: A vault versions history and keeps evidence with claims
vault.para: Every update to the observation history is a commit, so what the newsroom knew on any date can be recovered and compared. Records sit beside the observations that cite them. The read key is the only credential: anyone can open the desk, clone it with sgit, check each observation and rebuild it from its scripts.

yours.line: Swap the question, families and records for your beat
yours.para: The deck's closing brief is to choose a question, map the system, define its events and keep observing. In the vault that is one script, tools/build_data.py, so a hospital trust, port or river can replace the campus without changing the app. The hard editorial work is defining every event and its observable signal.

limits.line: Synthetic records, a partly invented atlas, no live watching
limits.para: Mesa Ranch and every name are invented. The deck gives 12 families and 12 examples; the other 66 event types were written for the vault. The desk works on fixed records, not live registries, and is a reading of Marconi's public slides, not his work or endorsed by him. Updated 15 October with graph pages.

sources.line: Sources: Marconi's slides, the Big Bend Sentinel, TechCrunch
sources.para: Requested on 15 October 2026 after reading Francesco Marconi's post and slides, When journalism becomes intelligence, from his INMA talk, and written and built by this site's agent the same day. Other sources are Rob D'Amico's Big Bend Sentinel report on the Pecos County data centre and TechCrunch on AppliedXL.
